name: Splenic Marginal Zone Lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of marked splenomegaly without significant lymphadenopathy
Bone marrow infiltration by small B-cells with marginal zone differentiation
Immunophenotyping showing CD19+, CD20+, CD5-, CD10-, CD23- B-cell population
Presence of villous lymphocytes in peripheral blood smear
Detection of NOTCH2 mutations or trisomy 3 in tumor cells

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of splenomegaly, bone marrow infiltration by marginal zone B-cells, and characteristic immunophenotype
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, morphological, immunophenotypic, and molecular findings.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of villous lymphocytes in peripheral blood
searchTerms: villous lymphocytes seen in blood test
peripheral blood with unusual lymphocyte shape
fatigue related to low red blood cells

occasional.symptomName: Abdominal discomfort or fullness due to splenomegaly
searchTerms: feeling of fullness or discomfort in abdomen from big spleen
belly discomfort related to enlarged spleen
swollen lymph nodes usually absent or minimal
little or no lymph node enlargement

rare.symptomName: Transformation to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
searchTerms: progression to aggressive large B-cell lymphoma
change to diffuse large B-cell cancer

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing villous lymphocytes
Cytopenias including anemia, thrombocytopenia, and leukopenia
Elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in some cases
imaging: Ultrasound or CT scan showing massive splenomegaly without significant lymphadenopathy
genetic: Somatic mutations in KLF2 and other genes associated with marginal zone lymphoma
other: Bone marrow biopsy demonstrating infiltration by small B-cells with marginal zone morphology
Immunophenotyping: CD19+, CD20+, CD5-, CD10-, CD23-

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of hairy cells with cytoplasmic projections
Positive for CD103 and annexin A1
Typically involves pancytopenia and bone marrow fibrosis
CD5 and CD23 positivity on B-cells
Primary involvement of lymph nodes rather than spleen
Histopathological differences in lymph node biopsy

redFlags: Development of B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
Signs of transformation to aggressive lymphoma (e.g., diffuse large B-cell lymphoma)
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
Chacón JI, et al. Splenic Marginal Zone Lymphoma: Clinical and Molecular Features. Blood Reviews. 2020.
